title: IL HB3851: SCH CD-CYBER-BULLYING

obligations: Each school district, charter school, and non-public non-sectarian elementary or secondary school shall create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying filed with the State Board of Education, based on the State Board's template and including the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d))

The policy or implementing procedure shall include a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within the permissible scope of the district's or school's jurisdiction and shall require that the district or school provide the victim with information regarding available services such as counseling, support services, and other programs (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
School personnel available for help with a bully or to make a report about bullying shall be made known to parents or legal guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d))

Every 2 years, each covered school shall conduct a review and re-evaluation of its policy and make necessary revisions; no later than September 30 of the subject year, the policy must be filed with the State Board of Education after being updated (Sec. 27-23.7(d))

The policy on bullying must include the bullying definition, statement that bullying is contrary to State law and policy consistent with subsection (a-5), procedures for promptly reporting bullying including identifying staff email and phone and anonymous reporting, procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved within 24 hours after administration is made aware, procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports including making all reasonable efforts to complete investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate support personnel, notifying principal or designee as soon as possible, providing parents and guardians information and opportunity to meet, interventions that can be taken, statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation, consequences and remedial actions for false accusation, engagement of stakeholders, posting on website and inclusion in handbook and distribution, policy evaluation process, consistency with school board policies, and requirement to report all individual instances of bullying and threats or self-harm to parents or legal guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying items (1)-(13))

School districts, charter schools, and non-public non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools shall collect, maintain, and submit to the State Board of Education non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying, in an annual report due no later than August 15 of each year starting with 2024-2025 through 2030-2031 (Sec. 27-23.7(f))

The State Board of Education shall adopt rules for submission of data including record of each verified allegation and action taken and whether based on actual or perceived characteristics, consistent with privacy laws (Sec. 27-23.7(f))

Upon request of a parent or legal guardian, the State Board of Education must provide non-identifiable data on number of bullying allegations and incidents in a given year in the school to the requesting parent or legal guardian (Sec. 27-23.7(g))
The State Board of Education shall adopt rules regarding handling of such data, maintaining privacy, and best practices for sharing numerical data with parents and legal guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(g))
By January 1, 2024, the State Board of Education shall post on its Internet website a template for a model bullying prevention policy (Sec. 27-23.7(h))

The State Board of Education shall monitor and provide technical support for implementation, review each filed policy to ensure it meets requirements including 13 criteria, provide written request for filing if missing, and publish notice of non-compliance on website if not filed within 14 days of request (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
prohibitions: Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of the aforementioned characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and non-public non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a))

No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or other school vehicles, at designated school bus stops, or at school-sponsored or school-sanctioned events or activities; through transmission of information from a school computer, school computer network, or similar electronic school equipment; or through transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location or use of technology or electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school if the bullying causes a substantial disruption to the educational process or orderly operation of a school (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4))

The policy on bullying must include a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and the consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person who engages in reprisal or retaliation (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(7))

Passed 2025-08-15. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Amends the Illinois School Code bullying prevention section to define bullying and cyber-bullying, including unauthorized digital replicas beginning in the 2026-2027 school year, and requires school districts, charter schools, and non-public non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools to create, implement, file, and periodically review bullying prevention policies, collect and report bullying data, and provide parent notifications and investigations.

Who it applies to

  • School districts
  • Charter schools
  • Non-public, non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools

Effective date

July 1, 2026 (Section 99)

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Bullying: includes cyber-bullying and means any severe or pervasive physical or verbal act or conduct, including communications made in writing or electronically, directed toward a student or students that has or can be reasonably predicted to have the effect of placing the student in reasonable fear of harm, causing a substantially detrimental effect on physical or mental health, substantially interfering with academic performance, or substantially interfering with ability to participate in or benefit from school services, activities, or privileges (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Cyber-bullying: bullying through the use of technology or any electronic communication, including transfer of signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, data, or intelligence by wire, radio, electromagnetic, photoelectronic, or photooptical systems, including electronic mail, Internet communications, instant messages, or facsimile communications; includes creation of a webpage or weblog impersonating another or knowing impersonation as author if creates bullying effects; includes distribution by electronic means to more than one person or posting on electronic medium accessible by one or more persons if creates bullying effects; beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, also includes posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if creates bullying effects (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Digital replica: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Policy on bullying: a bullying prevention policy that meets criteria including definition, statement contrary to law, reporting procedures, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation within 10 school days, involvement of support personnel, notification of principal, parent information and meeting, interventions, prohibition on reprisal, consequences for false accusation, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution, evaluation process, consistency, and reporting all instances and self-harm to parents (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Restorative measures: a continuum of school-based alternatives to exclusionary discipline that are adapted to school and community needs, contribute to school safety, protect positive learning climate, teach personal and interpersonal skills, build and restore relationships, reduce future disruption by balancing accountability with behavioral health needs, and increase student accountability if bullying based on religion, race, ethnicity, or other category identified in Illinois Human Rights Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • School personnel: persons employed by, on contract with, or who volunteer in a school district, charter school, or non-public non-sectarian elementary or secondary school, including administrators, teachers, school social workers, school counselors, school psychologists, school nurses, cafeteria workers, custodians, bus drivers, school resource officers, and security guards (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Unauthorized digital replica: the use of a digital replica of an individual without the consent of the depicted individual (Sec. 27-23.7(b))

Obligations

  • Each school district, charter school, and non-public non-sectarian elementary or secondary school shall create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying filed with the State Board of Education, based on the State Board's template and including the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • The policy or implementing procedure shall include a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within the permissible scope of the district's or school's jurisdiction and shall require that the district or school provide the victim with information regarding available services such as counseling, support services, and other programs (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • School personnel available for help with a bully or to make a report about bullying shall be made known to parents or legal guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Every 2 years, each covered school shall conduct a review and re-evaluation of its policy and make necessary revisions; no later than September 30 of the subject year, the policy must be filed with the State Board of Education after being updated (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • The policy on bullying must include the bullying definition, statement that bullying is contrary to State law and policy consistent with subsection (a-5), procedures for promptly reporting bullying including identifying staff email and phone and anonymous reporting, procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved within 24 hours after administration is made aware, procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports including making all reasonable efforts to complete investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate support personnel, notifying principal or designee as soon as possible, providing parents and guardians information and opportunity to meet, interventions that can be taken, statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation, consequences and remedial actions for false accusation, engagement of stakeholders, posting on website and inclusion in handbook and distribution, policy evaluation process, consistency with school board policies, and requirement to report all individual instances of bullying and threats or self-harm to parents or legal guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying items (1)-(13))
  • School districts, charter schools, and non-public non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools shall collect, maintain, and submit to the State Board of Education non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying, in an annual report due no later than August 15 of each year starting with 2024-2025 through 2030-2031 (Sec. 27-23.7(f))
  • The State Board of Education shall adopt rules for submission of data including record of each verified allegation and action taken and whether based on actual or perceived characteristics, consistent with privacy laws (Sec. 27-23.7(f))
  • Upon request of a parent or legal guardian, the State Board of Education must provide non-identifiable data on number of bullying allegations and incidents in a given year in the school to the requesting parent or legal guardian (Sec. 27-23.7(g))
  • The State Board of Education shall adopt rules regarding handling of such data, maintaining privacy, and best practices for sharing numerical data with parents and legal guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(g))
  • By January 1, 2024, the State Board of Education shall post on its Internet website a template for a model bullying prevention policy (Sec. 27-23.7(h))
  • The State Board of Education shall monitor and provide technical support for implementation, review each filed policy to ensure it meets requirements including 13 criteria, provide written request for filing if missing, and publish notice of non-compliance on website if not filed within 14 days of request (Sec. 27-23.7(d))

Prohibitions

  • Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of the aforementioned characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and non-public non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a))
  • No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or other school vehicles, at designated school bus stops, or at school-sponsored or school-sanctioned events or activities; through transmission of information from a school computer, school computer network, or similar electronic school equipment; or through transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location or use of technology or electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school if the bullying causes a substantial disruption to the educational process or orderly operation of a school (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4))
  • The policy on bullying must include a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and the consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person who engages in reprisal or retaliation (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(7))

Penalties and enforcement

The State Board of Education monitors implementation, reviews filed policies, requests filing if missing, and publishes notice of non-compliance on its website if a school fails to file within 14 days of written request (Sec. 27-23.7(d)). Schools not in compliance with subsection (f) data reporting are not eligible to receive a grant from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)). The Section does not create a private right of action; it states it shall not be interpreted to prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e)). No criminal or civil penalties are specified in this Section.

How it affects AI deployment

  • Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, cyber-bullying includes posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if it creates bullying effects; unauthorized digital replica means use of a digital replica of an individual without consent (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Schools must update their bullying prevention policies to include this expanded cyber-bullying definition and address unauthorized digital replicas, and must investigate and respond to reports of such conduct as bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d) and (b))
  • If an AI system is used to create or distribute unauthorized digital replicas of students or staff, that conduct may be treated as cyber-bullying under the policy, triggering reporting, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation within 10 school days, and possible interventions (Sec. 27-23.7(b) and (d))
  • Schools must collect and report non-identifiable data on verified allegations of bullying, which would include incidents involving unauthorized digital replicas (Sec. 27-23.7(f))
  • The definitions of artificial intelligence and digital replica are imported from the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act, so organizations should consult that Act for those terms (Sec. 27-23.7(b))

Notable exemptions

  • Nothing in this Section is intended to infringe upon any right to exercise free expression or the free exercise of religion or religiously based views protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution or under Section 3 of Article I of the Illinois Constitution (Sec. 27-23.7(a-5))
  • The prohibition on bullying through nonschool computers or devices applies only in cases in which a school administrator or teacher receives a report that bullying through this means has occurred and does not require a district or school to staff or monitor any nonschool-related activity, function, or program (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(4))
  • This Section shall not be interpreted to prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e))

Compliance steps

  • Review and update the bullying prevention policy to include the full statutory definition of bullying and cyber-bullying, including unauthorized digital replicas beginning 2026-2027, and ensure consistency with free expression protections (Sec. 27-23.7(b) and (a-5))
  • Include all required policy criteria: reporting procedures with staff contact and anonymous option, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation within 10 school days, involvement of support personnel, notification of principal, parent information and meeting, interventions, prohibition on retaliation, consequences for false accusation, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution, evaluation process, consistency, and reporting all instances and self-harm to parents (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying)
  • File the policy with the State Board of Education by September 30 of the subject year and every 2 years after review and revision (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Post the policy on the school's publicly accessible website, include it in the student handbook, post where other policies are posted, and distribute annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel including new employees (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(10))
  • Make known to parents, students, and school personnel which school personnel are available to help with a bully or to make a report (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Implement procedures to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within the school's jurisdiction and provide victims with information about available services (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Collect, maintain, and submit non-identifiable data on verified allegations of bullying annually by August 15, starting 2024-2025 through 2030-2031, following State Board rules (Sec. 27-23.7(f))
  • Conduct a policy evaluation process to assess outcomes and effectiveness, using relevant data, and make evaluation information available on the website or otherwise (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(11))
  • Provide evidence-based professional development and youth programming on bullying prevention, if desired (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Ensure compliance with State Board monitoring and respond to any written request for filing to avoid publication of non-compliance (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
